title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
statement_short: Given an array of 2D points representing spherical balloons where points[i] = [xstart, xend], find the minimum number of arrows that must be shot to burst all balloons. An arrow shot vertically upward along an x-coordinate bursts all balloons whose horizontal diameter overlaps that coordinate.
hint: Point count up to 10^5 dictates an O(n log n) algorithm by sorting interval end boundaries.
why_not: Right: Intervals sorting balloons by end coordinates shoots an arrow at the earliest ending point to greedily burst overlapping intervals in O(n log n) time. Not Two Pointers: Scanning unsorted interval boundaries with two pointers fails to identify global overlap endpoints. Not Binary Search: Point coordinates are unsorted and non-continuous, preventing binary searching on burst positions. Not Heap / Priority Queue: Storing coordinates in a min-heap costs O(n log n) time but adds unnecessary priority queue maintenance overhead.
complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space
